title: Artificial Intelligence in Alzheimer’s Disease: Evidence Maturity and Clinical Translation Across the Care Pathway
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) is now a credible translational research platform across the Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathway, but its clinical value is often difficult to judge from performance metrics alone. This scoping-informed methodological review maps AD-AI evidence across prevention and risk stratification, diagnosis and staging, treatment and therapeutic monitoring, and care and safety support, drawing on PubMed/MEDLINE, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, ScienceDirect/Scopus-indexed venues, Google Scholar, and citation chaining for literature from 2000 to May 2026. We contribute a decision-centered evidence-maturity framework and apply it to a diagnostic-anchored sample of 31 stage-specific appraisal entries from 29 unique reports, with a PROBAST+AI-informed diagnostic concern screen. Diagnostic AI provides the strongest current evidence base, while prevention, treatment, and care and safety applications show how AI can support earlier risk recognition, anti-amyloid workflow planning, longitudinal monitoring, and caregiver-facing safety systems. In the purposive appraisal sample, explicit reporting of calibration, decision-curve or net-benefit analysis, subgroup fairness, prospective workflow testing, and patient- or caregiver-centered endpoints was uncommon and, for several stage-specific items, absent; exact counts are reported in the appraisal table. The review argues that AD-AI is most persuasive when each model is linked to a user, decision, actionable threshold, uncertainty communication strategy, and outcome, supported by leakage-resistant validation, calibration, decision-curve assessment, subgroup testing, workflow evaluation, and lifecycle governance.
